It is the most successful club in the Czech Republic and one of the most successful in central Europe, winning the central European Cup (also known as the [[Mitropa Cup]]) three times and reaching the semi-finals of the European Cup (now the [[UEFA Champions League]]) in 1992 and the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] in 1973.{{cite web |url=http://www.sparta.cz/en/club/achievements.shtml |title=Achievements – AC Sparta Praha |publisher=Sparta.cz |access-date=13 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131118200618/http://www.sparta.cz/en/club/achievements.shtml |archive-date=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/teams/club=50033/profile/history/index.html |title=Sparta Praha – |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=16 September 1964 |access-date=13 November 2013 |archive-date=4 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104073350/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/teams/club=50033/profile/history/index.html |url-status=dead}} Sparta have won a record 38 domestic league titles,{{cite web|title=Sparta Prague Win 37th Czech Title After Nine Years Wait|url=https://www.praguemorning.cz/sparta-prague-win-37th-czech-title-after-nine-years-wait/|publisher=Prague Morning|date=2023-05-23|access-date=2023-05-28|archive-date=28 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528003300/https://www.praguemorning.cz/sparta-prague-win-37th-czech-title-after-nine-years-wait/|url-status=live}} a record 16 [[Czech Cup]]s (and its predecessor [[Czechoslovak Cup]]), and two [[Czech Supercup]]s. Sparta was long the main source for the [[Czech Republic national football team]]; however, lately the best Czech players almost exclusively play in foreign leagues. Sparta plays at Prague's [[Stadion Letná|Epet Arena]], also known as ''Letná Stadium''."}}
